newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU envoy wants to alter Mideast peace formula.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy wants to alter Mideast peace formula.

text.p: European Middle East peace envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos has said the best chance for Israel-Syria peace lay in a "total withdrawal for total security" deal rather than the "land for peace" formula now being touted.

"I have proposed to the presidency of the European Union, its member states and concerned parties in the Middle East that they change their approach on this question," Moratinos told the French news magazine L'Express in an interview published on Thursday.

"Until now, we were seeking a 'land for peace' formula but I suggest we replace it by a 'total withdrawal for total security' formula. Peace would come afterwards as a consequence of this equation," he said.

Syria and Israel have been been at odds for years about how to reach a settlement, with Israel demanding full peace, including diplomatic and other ties, and Syria demanding full Israeli withdrawal from the Golan heights captured in 1967.

Asked what advantages the parties would gain from his suggestion, Moratinos replied: "Advantages for everyone. Syria would regain the Golan and Israel would be ensured of safe borders and could settle the dramatic south Lebanon situation."
The Spanish diplomat said he agreed with France there should be a global settlement involving Syria, Lebanon and Israel and not bids for separate deals between Israel and the two Arab states.

"Of course, to reassure the Israelis, there should be solid formulas, guarantees of military presence and zones which would be demilitarised or zones of separation, or where there would be an international security presence," he said.
Moratinos said he disagreed with Arab states who said there could be no advances with Israel on economic, industrial or commercial projects until there was global peace in the region.
"That works against their own interests," he said, adding that European states could join such projects
Moratinos also said he trusted rightist Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to follow the path towards peace of assassinated Labour prime minister Yitzhak Rabin.

"Netanyahu probably has the capacity to rally to this goal those Israelis who are least convinced. With him, the peace process seems to me even more irreversible than before even if it still has to go through difficult phases," he said.

Moratinos said Netanyahu's decision to carry on with a controversial Jewish settlement around Arab East Jerusalem "undoubtedly does not go in the way of soothing things but let's not draw conclusions too hastily."
